messages:
maya: FYI — Sales just sent a dedicated capacity ask from AcmeCorp. They want predictable perf for a realtime chat product. Can we triage sizing + autoscale options?

rachel: Copy. Acme is asking for: 200 RPS steady, spikes to 400 RPS for 10m every hour, avg response size 120 tokens, p99 latency goal <250ms, and enterprise wants a monthly committed pool with burst credits. They asked for a cost ballpark by EOD.

jonah: Got it. Do we know what model family they're planning to run? That affects GPU choice / batch sizes. Also are these synchronous streaming chat requests or async batch generation?

rachel: Sales said "redwood-compat" model, probably a 13B dense variant (we should confirm). It's interactive chat (streaming), so latency matters.

leo: Quick napkin math: 200 steady RPS * 120 tokens ~= 24k tokens/sec overall. With streaming and low-latency, we can't heavily batch. On A10G-ish perf for a 13B, let's assume ~30-40 tokens/sec per GPU under our optimized runtime when prioritizing latency. That suggests ~600-800 GPUs if naive — which is obviously wrong because streaming/per-request parallelism differs. We need per-request latency profile.

jonah: Agree — need more concrete perf numbers. Can we ask Sales to confirm: avg tokens generated before first token (think first chunk latency), avg generation speed per request, and percentage of requests that use long context (>2048 tokens)?

maya: I'll ping the AE. Meanwhile, can infra propose a candidate autoscale policy and a conservative commit/burst model we could offer as a template?

leo: Proposed autoscale stub (for engineering discussion):
```
pool: acme-13b-prod
min_replicas: 3  # keep some warm capacity for tail latency
max_replicas: 40
target_rps_per_gpu: 6  # conservative for streaming, low-latency
burst_capacity: 8  # additional transient GPUs to handle hourly spikes
scale_cooldown_sec: 60
priority_policy: latency-first
```
This is intentionally conservative; we'd tune after benchmarks.

jonah: That target_rps_per_gpu=6 implies each GPU handles ~6 concurrent low-latency streams. For 200 steady RPS, with min_replicas 3 we'd be massively underprovisioned. Need to align numbers: 200 RPS / 6 = ~34 replicas required for steady state. So set min_replicas closer to 30 for committed capacity or offer a committed baseline + burst pool.

rachel: Customer prefers a smaller commit and burst credits rather than a giant monthly commit. They want predictability on p99 but won't sign for >30k/mo unless it's justified.

maya: Two options to present to customer: 1) Commit 30-35 GPUs with autoscale up to 50 (burst) — higher commit = lower unit cost, or 2) Commit 10-15 GPUs and include burst credits priced at premium. We should show cost delta and risk (p99 miss during spikes).

leo: I'll run microbenchmarks next 24h to get actual RPS-per-GPU for our 13B config (quantized int8 path + streaming). That will give better guidance.

jonah: Also surface the workload tuning levers to Acme: prefer shorter prefixes (reduce KV cache misses), enable client-side rate limiting, and set conservative max tokens per response. Those are cheaper than putting GPUs behind autoscale.

maya: Action items: (1) jonah/leo run perf tests and produce numbers by tomorrow noon; (2) maya to ask AE for model/context details and confirm traffic patterns; (3) rachel to draft two commercial options (commit vs commit+burst) with rough costs. I'll create a backlog ticket and mark P1.

rachel: +1. I'll attach customer slides and usage example once AE replies.

infra-bot: autoscaler: created provisional scaling policy draft (id: SP-9876) and saved to /internal/dedicated/sizing/SP-9876.

leo: Quick note for the spec doc — include rollback/fallback routes: route to smaller/cheaper model variant on sustained pressure, and cross-region fallback if a single region is capacity constrained. That avoids hard outages.

jonah: Also note KV prefix caching: if Acme can afford short-lived session affinity, we can cache KV per user which will cut compute by ~20-30% on repeated queries. Put that as a recommended config.

maya: Putting this into the product backlog: PD-2048. Include acceptance criteria: 1) benchmark report with RPS/GPU numbers; 2) recommended autoscale config for commit/burst options; 3) two commercial proposals + cost delta; 4) rollout playbook (fallback, monitoring, SLOs).

rachel: Sounds good. Can we promise EOD for the customer? We should say "estimate by tomorrow" until we have real numbers.

maya: Agreed. Tentative ETA: numbers tomorrow noon, proposal EOD tomorrow.

jonah: If perf tests show better throughput we can shrink commit and sell the burst credits option. If worse, we'll recommend higher commit or mixing model quantization.

rachel: I'll keep Acme warm but tell them we'll follow up with a formal proposal tomorrow.

maya: Thanks team. I'll link PD-2048 when created. :thumbsup:
